browser.description: Browser webviews (label browser-*) hold an empty capability set: no invoke, no event listeners, no filesystem, no shell. This file exists to declare that deny-by-default posture in the open — a label no capability mentions would be equally safe and much easier to widen by accident. src-tauri/src/browser.rs parses this file and fails the build's test leg if any permission is ever added here, or if any other capability's window/webview globs start reaching browser labels.

default.description: Default capability: the main window may invoke the engine-bridge commands, and nothing else. The `shell` permission set (src-tauri/permissions/shell.json) is this app's ACL manifest — before it existed, Tauri let a *local*-origin invoke of any `codify_*` command through with no capability check at all, which is the bypass this capability now closes. It names the thirteen commands one by one rather than granting a wildcard, and `windows` is `["main"]` so nothing reaches a `browser-*` webview. No shell or filesystem scope is granted: the frontend only uses `invoke`, and the engine is spawned by the Rust backend over tokio, not through the shell plugin.
